EXPLANATION: The strong band at 2233 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a nitrile ν(C≡N); the spectrum also shows clear aromatic signatures: a strong ring C=C stretch at 1610 cm⁻¹, para-disubstituted benzene ring modes near 822 and 801 cm⁻¹, and both aromatic and aliphatic C–H stretches at 3073 and 2930 cm⁻¹ (supported by GFQ-003). The methyl deformation at 1382 cm⁻¹ and in-plane aromatic C–H bending around 1180–1200 cm⁻¹ further fit a methyl-substituted benzonitrile. Absence of a strong carbonyl band near 1700 cm⁻¹ disfavors ester/aldehyde-containing candidates (1, 3, 4, 10); the CN frequency is higher than typical thiocyanates, disfavoring 5. Overall, Cc1ccc(C#N)cc1 (a p-methylbenzonitrile) best matches the Raman features.
